headline: High-risk overlap: both agents can write shared files and run shells, while nullclaw’s broad network/MCP and ms-swift’s file-based workflows create leakage, conflict, and cascading-error pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ms-swift reads/writes files and processes stdin/stdout, while nullclaw has workspace files, browser, webhook, and MCP surfaces. If nullclaw passes untrusted content into ms-swift’s file or stdin path, prompt injection is plausible in default workflows. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF nullclaw forwards webhook, browser, or MCP content into ms-swift stdin or files without sanitization
IF ms-swift treats workspace text as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and instruction/data separator in the handoff prompt
Strip tool directives from inbound text before passing to ms-swift
Use a read-only staging file for untrusted content
Disable MCP routes that can inject arbitrary text into the shared workflow
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and instruction filtering

B_data_leakage.rationale: ms-swift handles hub_token and sdk-token and can read/write files; nullclaw handles API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, and workspace files, plus broad network egress. In a shared workspace or handoff, sensitive material can flow from one agent into the other and then out over nullclaw’s network surfaces. The default blast radius includes secrets exfiltration.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or config directory
IF either agent loads secrets from files into its context window
mitigations: Store secrets in separate per-agent directories
Rotate any shared tokens before pairing
Mount secret files read-only for the non-owning agent
Block outbound network for the agent that should not exfiltrate
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent secret isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shells, spawn subprocesses, read and write filesystems, and nullclaw can modify git state. If they share a directory, concurrent writes or git operations can corrupt state or overwrite each other’s outputs. Because nullclaw supports multiple instances and shared durable memory, coordination is not guaranteed by default.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF either agent performs git operations or file rewrites without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Disable git writes for the pair run
Use file locks around shared artifacts
Serialize shell tasks that touch the same paths
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: ms-swift can emit model outputs from files and stdin/stdout, and nullclaw has browser, webhook, schedule, and delegate-style tool surfaces. If nullclaw consumes ms-swift output as authoritative, it can trigger downstream actions or web requests based on unverified content. That creates a classic cascading-error path with potentially irreversible external effects.
conditions: IF nullclaw uses ms-swift output as a source for webhook, browser, or delegate actions
IF no verification step checks ms-swift’s claims before action
mitigations: Require human review before any external action
Add a verification step that cross-checks outputs against source files
Disable delegate/webhook actions for the first run
Log and diff all model-generated claims before execution
requires-engineering: add policy gates for action-taking tools

E_compliance.rationale: ms-swift touches datasets, checkpoints, logs, and configuration data, while nullclaw handles API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, and audit logs. If regulated or customer data is placed into the shared workflow, differing retention and logging practices can create compliance gaps. The profiles do not show a specific residency mismatch, so medium is the highest supported level.
conditions: IF regulated customer data or secrets are processed by both agents
IF their logs or workspace retention policies differ
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair run
Purge logs after the session
Separate audit logs from content files
Document retention for each workspace
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies
